angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 403,506 km at 29.65 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 33.7247 +/- 0.0169 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 29.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.58 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Passegger et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 9827 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..22P/abstract): 403,506 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.62 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Passegger et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 9827 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..22P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4236 +/- 12 K from Passegger et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 9827 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..22P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Passegger et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 9827 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..22P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-9827.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.704, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
